 Order

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C has been filed seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.228/2019 PS: Udaypura, Raisen registered under Section 498A, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. It is contended by the counsel that the present applicants are being prosecuted in respect of aforesaid offences as a result of which, FIR was lodged by respondent No.2 who is the wife of applicant No.1.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that respondent No.2 in the FIR alleging inter alia that after her marriage with applicant No.1 in the year 2016, she was subjected to harassment under the garb of demand of dowry, then the respondent No.2 came to her paternal house at Udaypura.
The applicants even reached at the paternal house of the respondent No.2 and she was beaten mercilessly there as well.

It is contended by the counsel that the prosecution is unsustainable inasmuch as, the marriage between applicant No.1 and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 27/11/2016 and as without assigning any reasons, respondent No.2 refused to reside with applicant No.1, then an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of Conjugal Rights was filed.
The said application was allowed vide order dated 08/05/2018.
Thereafter, with an oblique motive, FIR dated 05/11/2019 has been lodged.

4. It is contended by the counsel that lodging of FIR was merely an afterthought and no specific allegations have been levelled against the applicants and only general and omnibus allegations have been levelled against them.

It is further contended by the counsel that there is an MLC report on record which reflects that no fresh external injury was found on the body of respondent No.2 and therefore, the allegation of marpeet on 30/06/2019 was baseless and patently false.

Learned counsel has placed reliance on the decision of this Court in the case of Bhupendra Singh Notey and Ors. Vs.
The State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State and respondent No.2 has opposed the aforesaid prayer while submitting that the FIR contains specific allegation against the applicants.
The applicants on 30/06/2019 manhandled the respondent No.2 and the incident was witnessed by the neighbours as well.
Thus, as there are specific allegations against the applicants in the FIR, the present petition filed by the applicants deserves to be dismissed.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has placed reliance on the decisions of Apex Court in the cases of Taramani Prakash Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors. reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260, Central Bureau of Investigation Vs. Aryan Singh reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 292 and Pratibha Vs. Rameshwari Devi and Ors. reported in (2007)
12 SCC 369.

7. Heard rival submissions of the parties and perused the record.
8.

A perusal of the record reflects that respondent No.2 lodged an FIR with the allegations that after her marriage with applicant No.1 in 2016, when respondent No.2 came to her matrimonial house,
she was subjected to torture and cruelty under the garb of demand of dowry by the present applicants and time and again, she was tortured in view of the aforesaid demands.

Her husband,
Nand (sister-in-law) and Jethani (sister-in-law) also slapped her on many occasions and she was not been given food as well.

Thereafter, she was thrown out of her matrimonial house and then she started residing with her father at Kuchwara, Bamhori, then the present applicants came on 30/06/2019 at respondent No.2's paternal house and again they manhandled her.
The said incident was witnessed by two neighbours namely Pawan Sahu and Hoshiyar Dhakad.
9. A perusal of the record reflects that the said incident was witnessed by aforesaid two neighbours whose statements recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. are available on record.
After lodging of FIR the respondent No.2 was referred for Medical Examination and the MLC was given on 05/11/2019.

Undisputedly as per the FIR the allegation of manhandling were pertaining to 30/06/2019 therefore, there was no question of any fresh injury on 05/11/2019, thus, prima facie considering the nature of allegations which are levelled in the FIR and also considering the statements of neighbours which refer to an incident dated 30/06/2019, this Court is not inclined to entertain this petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C as there are specific allegations pertaining to specific date as well as place and there are statements of witnesses/neighbors corroborating the factum of alleged incident.
10.
In view of the aforesaid, no interference is warranted in the matter.
The judgment relied by the petitioner is factually distinguishable.
11. Accordingly, this petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C stands dismissed.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE Astha Rajendra @ Ram Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50882733/
